clue.text: Enlisted man to study the lines

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
an actor's lines make up the script

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to learn his lines, as if drafted into a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscript is a person called up and enrolled for compulsory military service.

clue.text: Start with unpopular team

parts.note: out of favour or out of fashion means unpopular
a set is a group playing together, as in tennis sets of players or a side

explanation.surface: A season beginning with a team nobody likes.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset is the very beginning of something, its commencement.

clue.text: Traffic light lags in changing

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traffic light is slow to change colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is part of the fodder: LAGS IN gives six letters, rearranged by 'changing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic light is a road signal that tells drivers when to stop and go.

clue.text: Get better going round the East-is that so?

indicators.note: going round says the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to rally is to recover or improve after illness
E is the standard abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Someone asks in surprise whether recovery really comes by travelling round the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Really? is an exclamation of surprise or doubt, asking if something is true.

clue.text: An unexpected dip in the road, and one may tip right out of the window

definitions.text: An unexpected dip in the road

indicators.note: tip ... out of means one piece is tipped out, removed from the window word
out of, with tip, says a letter leaves the word for the window

parts.note: a porthole is a round window in a ship's side

explanation.surface: A hole in the road, and a passenger might tip out through the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip ... out of' removes R from PORTHOLE, a ship's window.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a hollow in a road surface that jolts a passing vehicle.

clue.text: Pick up pieces in smaller quantities for such a dress?

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: parts are pieces
less means in smaller quantities

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a dress made with less fabric is the result of picking up scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' is a reversal signal only because this is a down entry: lifting the word makes it read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapless dress has no shoulder straps, staying up on its own.

clue.text: Unable to speak-discovered in shock

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak
found means discovered

explanation.surface: Someone is struck speechless on being found out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dumbfounded is to be astonished; here the word stands for stunned and amazed.

clue.text: With cause for complaint, give grade poorly

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters of give grade are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A student has grounds to grumble when a teacher marks badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggrieved means feeling wronged, with a grievance to air.

clue.text: Nervous, when thus highly extended

explanation.surface: A tense person is stretched taut, highly strung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly strung' means nervous, so the word alone fills the gap; it also means stretched out, like a string.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly strung describes a tense, excitable person; strung on its own means stretched tight or extended in a line.

clue.text: Buck House the place for men to hold this?

definitions.text: Buck House the place for men to hold this?

parts.words: Buck House the place for men to hold this?
parts.note: Buck House is the nickname for Buckingham Palace, the royal residence in London; read literally, a buck's house is where males gather for a pre-wedding celebration

explanation.surface: Buckingham Palace imagined as the venue for an all-male party.
explanation.walkthrough: Buck House is British slang for Buckingham Palace; read as a male deer (stag) plus house (party gathering).
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party is a celebration for a groom and his male friends before a wedding.

clue.text: Anaesthetist's prattle

explanation.surface: An anaesthetist chatters away to the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive reads as belonging to the anaesthetist, but it stands for 'anaesthetist is', defining a giver of jabs, an injector.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gives injections could be called a jabber; jabber also means rapid, meaningless chatter.

clue.text: Commemorative coin for special old menial

indicators.note: special hints the letters of old menial are to be made into something different

explanation.surface: A coin is struck to honour an old servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a large medal, often struck to mark an event or person.

clue.text: Retreat, getting some special cover

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone retreats, taking special cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess in a room, a secluded nook to withdraw into.

clue.text: Punter's away, having made a profit

parts.note: a punter is one who bets, a better
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: A gambler has gone home after a winning day.
explanation.definitionFit: Better off means richer, in an improved financial position.

clue.text: Good hand of cards is what landlady likes

explanation.surface: A poker hand compared to a guest-house owner's ideal night.
explanation.walkthrough: A landlady running a guest house wants every room taken.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, three of a kind plus a pair is a strong hand; a theatre or lodging with every place occupied is also so described.

clue.text: Reckless type did reveal problems

indicators.note: problems suggests the letters of did reveal are in trouble and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A thrill-seeker exposed the difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a person who takes wild risks for the thrill.

clue.text: Litter in part of garden

explanation.surface: Rubbish thrown into a flower patch.
explanation.walkthrough: Litter here is straw bedding for animals, not rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is straw laid down for animals to sleep on; a flower patch in a garden is also so called.

clue.text: Ask for book, for example

explanation.surface: Someone requests a book, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to plead or request earnestly.

clue.text: Pat's awful upbringing

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up reverses the word, so it reads upwards

parts.note: bad means awful

explanation.surface: Pat had a terrible childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat looks like a person's name; it is the verb, to tap lightly. 'upbringing' turns BAD upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To dab is to touch lightly, like a gentle tap.

clue.text: Big bird gets behind rival

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
late means behind time

explanation.surface: A large bird falls behind its competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to equal or surpass them.

clue.text: Proverbial state encouraging greater fondness

parts.note: refers to the proverb that being away makes the heart grow fonder

explanation.surface: A nod to an old saying about love growing at a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence means being away, which the saying claims makes the heart grow fonder.

clue.text: Sack rejected for idle talk

indicators.note: rejected suggests something sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a bag is a sack

explanation.surface: Someone gets fired for chatting idly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like dismissal but is a bag; 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gab is casual chatter, as in the gift of the gab.

clue.text: Godless person hates it getting out

indicators.note: getting out hints the letters of hates it break free and rearrange

explanation.surface: An unbeliever hates having to go out.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist is one who believes there is no god.

clue.text: Bank clerk who can't keep a confidence?

explanation.surface: A cashier who gossips about customers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: one who tells secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashier at a bank counter has this title; a blabbermouth who tells things is also one.

clue.text: Charm of a stubborn person beginning to tire

parts.note: a mule is proverbially obstinate, so a stubborn person is called one

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The appeal of a stubborn type who is starting to flag.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil.

clue.text: Georgia has folk tales in abundance

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
lore is traditional knowledge, folk tales and beliefs

explanation.surface: Georgia is rich in folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore means in plenty, placed after its noun.

clue.text: Dabble in stockmarket — lost one's shirt?

explanation.surface: A gambler on shares loses everything.
explanation.walkthrough: To lose one's shirt is to lose all one's money; read literally, one is left wearing a vest.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to put money into shares; someone stripped of a shirt is left in a vest, an undershirt.

clue.text: After tea with politician, Agnes couldn't finish the bubbly

indicators.note: after says the next piece follows the first ones

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
MP is Member of Parliament

indicators.note: couldn't finish means the last letter of Agnes is dropped

explanation.surface: Agnes, having had tea with an MP, leaves her sparkling wine unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbly is informal for sparkling wine, chiefly from France's Champagne region.

clue.text: Hordes travel to this Greek island

indicators.note: travel suggests the letters of hordes move around

explanation.surface: Crowds of tourists head to a Greek isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is the largest of the Dodecanese islands in the Aegean.

clue.text: Determination was Shakespeare's strength

parts.note: Will is the familiar name of William Shakespeare
power means strength

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's great strength was his resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Willpower is resolve, the strength of mind to carry something through.

clue.text: Sign that rock has not always been so lifeless?

definitions.text: Sign that rock has not always been so lifeless?

parts.words: Sign that rock has not always been so lifeless?
parts.note: describes evidence preserved in stone of a creature that once lived

explanation.surface: A geologist ponders evidence that stone once held life.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the preserved remains or trace of an ancient organism in rock.

clue.text: Law about film getting Oscar, for example

indicators.note: about says the law word goes round the film

parts.note: a statute is a written law
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A law concerning which film wins an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' works as a container signal here, not as 'concerning'; E.T. is the 1982 Spielberg film, a common crossword abbreviation for film.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is the small gold figure awarded at the Academy Awards.
